articles.title: A 'kiss' too costly? 3,400 lipstick marks, Rs 5,500 fine; why defacing your car may land you in trouble
articles.summary: A splash of lipstick or a bold vinyl sticker might seem like a harmless way to make your ride stand out. But when does personalising a car cross the l.
articles.body: A splash of lipstick or a bold vinyl sticker might seem like a harmless way to make your ride stand out. But when does personalising a car cross the line into a traffic violation? In Gwalior, 3,400 lipstick marks on a car landed its driver a 5,500 challan, turning an unusual makeover into a traffic-rule headache and highlighting the legal risks of vehicle customisation.My car, my rules? Delhi no stranger to this fictionA search of Delhi-based car-sticker and accessories shops, along with social media handles promoting such work, throws up a range of examples:Some offer to change only a section of a car’s colour, such as turning part of an orange car blackSome convert a white car to black by full-body wrapOthers advertise full-body vinyl wraps, cars split between their original colour and a contrasting shade and giant graphics, such as a red lion covering a substantial part of the bodyStickers for windows, windshields and other prominent surfaces are also widely promotedUse of designations like ‘Police’, ‘Army’, ‘Press’, or fake govt logos on private vehicles is rampantUse of caste stickers like Brahman, Yadav, Gujjar, Jaat, Rajput and others on cars has also gained tractionSmall decorative stickers may be permitted on body panels as long as they do not obscure the base colour, registration details or safety reflectorsBut where does this personalisation endAsk whether all this is legal, the answers begin to differ. One shopkeeper said RTO permission is required for such modifications, but added that many customers do not bother getting it. “Our job is to tell customers when they ask. We have told you now; what you do after that is up to you,” he said. Another took a more relaxed view, claiming that if only around 30% of the car’s body is covered, it would not be illegal and would not attract a challan.What the rulebook statesSection 52 of the MV Act defines an alteration as “a change in the structure of a vehicle which results in a change in its basic feature.” It says an owner cannot alter a vehicle in a way that makes the particulars in the RC differ from those originally specified by the manufacturer. The RC records key details, including the vehicle’s colour, making a change potentially actionable. The law provides certain exceptions in specified engine modifications. Where an alteration is permitted, the owner must report it to the registering authority within 14 days and submit the RC along with the prescribed fee.What happens if you violate itSection 182A(4) provides for imprisonment of up to six months or a fine of Rs 5,000 for altering a vehicle in a manner not permitted under the Act.Section 177 provides a Rs 500 first-offence penalty where an MV Act violation has no specific punishment.What experts sayWhile owners may view a sticker or wrap as a cosmetic change, traffic police assess modifications in terms of vehicle identity, visibility and road safety. Officials say vehicles carrying large banners or other forms of visual defacement, including those spotted around Delhi University, are also challaned.Section 52 of MV Act bars alterations that make a vehicle’s particulars differ from those specified by the manufacturer and recorded in the RC. While not every cosmetic change is a violation, modifications that obstruct visibility, alter the vehicle’s identity or distract the driver or other road users can pose a safety risk and invite action. Traffic police also challan vehicles with vinyl graphics, large stickers covering around 30–60% of the body and other unauthorised modifications. Other common violations include tinted or sun-control films, defective or non-standard number plates and modifications that can obstruct visibility or distract other road users, saidDinesh Kumar Gupta, Additional CP TrafficSection 52 bars alterations that change a vehicle’s particulars from those recorded by the manufacturer, but the law does not specify how much of a vehicle can be covered by a different colour or graphic. The RC clearly records whether a vehicle is single-tone or dual-tone. So, if a black car is wrapped to appear black and red, it can be treated as a violation. Similarly, an orange-and-black car should have both colours reflected in the RC. RTO permission is required for permitted alterations, though private owners rarely seek it, said Anil Chikhara, former Delhi transport commissionerGwalior examplePolice in Gwalior recently seized a car covered in 3,400 lipstick marks allegedly left by the owner’s girlfriend as part of a social media stunt.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: In 1921, girl buried 3,500 years ago in Denmark was found with a strange drink, unusual clothes and a child’s bones; archaeologists still wonder who she was
articles.summary: Europe News: In 1921, the excavation of a burial mound near Egtved in Denmark brought an extraordinary Bronze Age story back into view. Inside a sealed oak coffin .
articles.body: In 1921, the excavation of a burial mound near Egtved in Denmark brought an extraordinary Bronze Age story back into view. Inside a sealed oak coffin lay the remains of a young woman who had been buried around 1370 BC, along with clothing, jewellery, tools and a small bark bucket. The discovery was remarkable because the coffin had protected fragile materials that would normally disappear over thousands of years. According to the National Museum of Denmark, the girl was about 16 to 18 years old when she died, and only parts of her hair, brain, teeth, nails and skin survived. Her unusual clothes and burial objects have since offered clues about Bronze Age rituals and everyday life, making her one of Denmark’s most famous prehistoric figures ever found.What was found inside the ancient coffin of DenmarkThe Egtved Girl was buried inside an oak coffin beneath a barrow known as Storehøj, near Egtved, west of Vejle. The National Museum of Denmark states that she was laid to rest around 1370 BC, meaning the burial was almost 3,500 years old when archaeologists opened it in 1921. The coffin had preserved a surprisingly detailed picture of the young woman and the objects placed with her. Her clothing included a short tunic and a knee-length skirt made from cords. A large bronze belt plate decorated with spirals rested on her stomach, while bronze rings were found around her arms and another slender ring was worn in her ear. A horn comb was attached to her belt, and a small bark box near her face contained a bronze awl and remains of a hair net. At her feet was another bark container that had once held a fermented drink. The burial also contained a small bundle of clothing and cremated bones belonging to a child aged around five or six. Some additional bones from the same child were found inside the bark box. The discovery therefore left archaeologists curious about the people connected to the burial.What did the Bronze Age drink reveal about that eraPerhaps one of the most unexpected clues came from the small bark bucket placed near the Egtved Girl's feet. When researchers examined the thick brown material remaining at the bottom, they found evidence that the container had held a fermented drink. According to the National Museum of Denmark, the drink was probably a type of beer sweetened with honey. It appears to have been made using cowberries or cranberries, while wheat grains, bog myrtle and large amounts of pollen were also detected. The pollen was particularly useful. The museum explains that pollen can act like a fingerprint for plants, allowing researchers to identify some of the ingredients that were present in the ancient drink. What might initially have looked like a dark residue therefore became evidence of how people prepared beverages more than three millennia ago. The find also shows how much information can remain hidden in ordinary burial objects. The bucket itself was simple, but its contents preserved details about plants, food and drink that would otherwise have been lost.Importance of the girl’s unusual skirtThe Egtved Girl's clothing has become one of the most recognisable features of the burial. According to the National Museum of Denmark, the skirt was about 38 centimetres long, reached the knees and was wound twice around her waist. It was made from cords rather than woven cloth and was part of a style that was used throughout the Bronze Age. The skirt may have been more than everyday clothing. Small bronze female figures discovered at Grevensvænge in Zealand were also shown wearing similar cord skirts. The museum notes that these figures have been interpreted as representing rituals performed during Bronze Age religious feasts. One assumption is that women wearing these skirts may have taken part in ritual dances. If that is correct, the Egtved Girl's clothing could offer more than a glimpse of Bronze Age fashion. It could also hint at activities in which she may have participated during her lifetime. The National Museum of Denmark presents it as a possibility rather than a certainty. Still, the connection between the skirt and ritual imagery gives the simple-looking garment an intriguing meaning.Unfolding the Bronze Age with this unique burial in DenmarkThe Egtved Girl's grave provides a rare glimpse into a period when clothing, jewellery, ritual and burial customs were closely connected. Her bronze belt plate, decorated with spirals, may have represented the sun, which the National Museum of Denmark describes as the most important element in Bronze Age religion. Her grave also demonstrates how carefully certain individuals could be prepared for burial. She was placed in an oak coffin with clothing, personal items, a drink and other objects. The survival of these materials has allowed researchers to move beyond studying bones only and consider aspects of Bronze Age life that are normally difficult to recover. The discovery at Egtved shows how a single well-preserved burial can turn an otherwise distant period of history into something remarkably human.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: CBC tells journalists not to call 9/11 ‘terrorist attacks’ in internal guidance
articles.summary: The Canadian Broadcasting Corporation memo told staff not to call 9/11 a terrorist attack ahead of the 25th anniversary, sparking political backlash.
articles.body: The Canadian Broadcasting Corporation on Thursday defended an internal memo directing its reporters and editors to refrain from describing the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks as "terrorist attacks," telling Fox News Digital the guidance reflected its longstanding practice of attributing terms it considers politically and emotionally loaded. "It is the practice of the CBC to exercise extreme caution before using the words ‘terrorist’ and ‘terrorism,'" CBC Public Affairs Director Kerry Kelly said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "The memo was a reminder of the longstanding practice that favours the use of these terms with attribution in our reporting." The memo was authored by Basem Boshra, CBC News' senior director of journalistic standards and public trust, and surfaced ahead of the attacks' 25th anniversary. The directive was first reported by Toronto Sun columnist Warren Kinsella, who said it was addressed to CBC News staff. "Do not refer to the Sept. 11 attacks as terrorist attacks," the memo said. SMITHSONIAN-LINKED MUSEUM IN EL-SAYED’S BACKYARD PUTS AMERICA’S POST-9/11 RESPONSE ON TRIAL The memo instead described the events as hijackings that led to passenger jet crashes in Washington, D.C., Pennsylvania and Manhattan. It also said the World Trade Center was destroyed. New York City Councilwoman Vickie Paladino condemned the guidance in a statement to Fox News Digital, accusing the broadcaster of disregarding the victims of the attacks and deliberately undermining the historical record. "The CBC guidance is frankly outrageous and insulting, but it stands as a stark warning for what happens when you allow institutions of public trust to be taken over by leftists and foreign interests," Paladino said. "This is not merely a callous disregard for the memory of those who perished on 9/11, it is a deliberate effort to undermine the fundamental truth of what happened that day in direct service to Islamism, as Europe, Canada, and the United States become increasingly overwhelmed by Islamist politics. We must not tolerate it any longer and dedicate ourselves to fighting this poison with every tool we have available before it’s too late," she continued. I LOST MY WIFE ON 9/11. PLEASE LET THIS 25TH ANNIVERSARY BELONG TO THE FAMILIES Conservative Canadian MP Rachael Thomas, who represents Lethbridge, Alberta, called the guidance "absolutely shameful" in a statement posted on X. "The CBC is choosing to redefine terrorism in a way that downplays the atrocity of 9/11. Refusing to call it an act of terrorism dishonors the victims, their families, the survivors, and the first responders who witnessed the horrors of that day. 9/11 was an act of terrorism. Full stop," Thomas said. The Centre for Israel and Jewish Affairs also criticized the memo, characterizing the description of the attacks as "hijackings that led to crashes" as "sanitizing" history and a "collapse of journalistic standards." Kelly pointed Fox News Digital to a 2023 editor’s blog in which CBC News general manager and editor-in-chief Brodie Fenlon explained that the broadcaster focused on documenting violent events while declining to independently apply terrorism labels. "We bear witness. But CBC News does not itself designate specific groups as terrorists, or specific acts as terrorism, regardless of the region or the events, because these words are so loaded with meaning, politics and emotion that they can end up being impediments to our journalism," Fenlon said. 9/11 VICTIM'S IDENTITY EMERGES NEARLY 25 YEARS LATER AFTER DNA BREAKTHROUGH CRACKS MYSTERY The public guidance specifically said CBC preferred "the Sept. 11 attacks" or similar language. It applied the same approach to the 2005 London bombings, the 2004 Madrid train bombings and the 2011 bombing at a Moscow airport, unless the terrorism label was attributed. The FBI described 9/11 as the most lethal terrorist attacks in history. Nineteen al Qaeda terrorists hijacked four airliners, killing nearly 3,000 people and triggering the largest investigation in FBI history. Canada’s government also lists Al Qaida as a terrorist entity and states that the organization perpetrated the World Trade Center and Pentagon attacks. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The guidance echoed a CBC controversy following Hamas’ Oct. 7, 2023, attack on Israel. Fox News Digital reported that an internal email instructed journalists not to call militants or soldiers "terrorists" and to frame the term as an attributed opinion. CBC confirmed that email and defended the policy as consistent with practices at other news organizations.

articles.title: Phoenix expanded heat relief in 2026 after dangerous gaps in 2024 pushed the city toward 24/7 cooling and overnight respite
articles.summary: US News: Phoenix took a step in protecting residents from extreme desert heat in 2024, when it began providing overnight heat respite for people who could not .
articles.body: Phoenix took a step in protecting residents from extreme desert heat in 2024, when it began providing overnight heat respite for people who could not rely on cooling centres after normal hours. The move came as the city faced dangerous summer conditions, exposing a gap in a heat relief system that often operated only during daytime and business hours. According to the City of Phoenix's 2025 Heat Response Plan, this created “gaps in network availability, particularly in the late afternoon and evening hours, as well as on weekends”. Phoenix’s response was to keep cool spaces available beyond those limits, giving people somewhere to escape the heat during the late afternoon, evening and overnight. The first overnight locations, including Burton Barr Library and Senior Opportunities West Senior Centre, helped shape an approach to round-the-clock heat protection. By 2025, the city had built on that experience with a 24/7 Heat Respite and Navigation Centre at 20 W. Jackson Street, combining a cool refuge with water and services for people experiencing homelessness. The initiative became a key part of Phoenix’s heat strategy.Phoenix expanded its 24/7 heat relief services in 2026Phoenix further expanded its heat-response system under its 2026 Heat Response Plan, approved by the Mayor and City Council in February 2026. The city continued operating the 24/7 Heat Respite and Navigation Centre at 20 W. Jackson Street and added a partnership with Justa Centre at 1001 W. Jefferson St., offering cooling centre hours from 3 pm to 9 pm. Both sites provide cool indoor space, navigation services and transport to shelters or other services for people experiencing homelessness. Phoenix also extended Cholla Library’s cooling hours until 9 pm Monday to Saturday and from noon to 9 pm on Sundays and holidays. A new referral partnership with UMOM New Day Centres was also planned to provide heat respite and links to services for families with minor children experiencing homelessness.From cooling centres to a broader heat-safety networkThe 2026 plan also placed greater emphasis on prevention and community outreach. Phoenix allocated $450,000 in FEMA Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities grant funding to train public-facing city employees to connect residents with heat-related services. The American Red Cross was set to conduct outreach in mobile-home and senior communities, while Park Stewards and Community Emergency Response Team volunteers would provide heat-safety information and cold water at Camelback Mountain, Piestewa Peak and South Mountain trailheads. The measures followed a second consecutive year of declining heat-related deaths in Maricopa County, with confirmed deaths in 2025 about 30% lower than in 2024. Together, the changes showed how Phoenix was moving beyond daytime cooling centres towards a wider system of 24/7 respite, extended opening hours, transport, shelter connections and community outreach.How Phoenix heat relief services faced gaps during extreme heat in 2024Phoenix's heat response had already included indoor cooling centres and hydration stations, but these services did not always cover the hours when extreme temperatures remained dangerous. The 2025 plan explains that participating Heat Relief Network facilities “typically provide services coincident with their normal hours of business operation”, leaving gaps later in the day and at weekends.The 2025 plan described summer 2024 as “the hottest in the City’s history”, while the season also set records for the number of days reaching 110°F, nights remaining above 90°F and consecutive days reaching at least 100°F.New heat centre builds on Phoenix’s 24/7 respite servicesThe city's 2025 plan says the new centre would “improve 24/7 heat respite capacity from the 2024 heat season”, building on the overnight and 24-hour services provided at Burton Barr and Senior Opportunities West. These locations provided an alternative when other cooling services were unavailable, helping people remain indoors and away from the heat for longer periods. The city’s 2025 plan says those two locations would return to their normal roles as cooling and hydration sites during regular operating hours.The 2024 experience also showed that heat relief needed to be connected with other forms of support. In its updated approach, Phoenix planned not only to provide a cool indoor refuge but also water, navigation assistance and transport for people experiencing homelessness, allowing visitors to connect with wider city services.Phoenix opened a dedicated 24/7 Heat Respite and Navigation Centre in 2025Building on the 2024 experience, Phoenix opened a dedicated 24/7 Heat Respite and Navigation Centre at 20 W. Jackson Street for the 2025 heat season. The centre was chosen for its accessibility to people travelling on foot or by bicycle and its proximity to public transport, with Community Bridges and the Phoenix Police Department providing staffing and security. Phoenix described it as a continuation of the previous year’s effort, offering a cool indoor space and water overnight, along with navigation and transport resources for people experiencing homelessness.The 24/7 centre was not intended to replace Phoenix’s wider network of cooling centres, libraries and hydration stations but to fill gaps when other services were unavailable. In 2025, the city also extended the hours of Cholla, Harmon and Yucca libraries until 10 pm, including Sundays and holidays. Together, these measures formed part of Phoenix’s broader heat strategy, which included 30 heat-response actions across eight strategies, covering public cooling spaces, drinking water, safer homes, worker protection, community outreach and coordination with external agencies.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Rape and sex offence specialists on all police forces by 2027, PM says
articles.summary: The plans for forces in England and Wales had been scheduled to be rolled out by summer 2029, but have been brought forward.
articles.body:
Investigators specialising in rape and sex offences will be introduced to every police force in England and Wales by the end of 2027, the government has said.

Ministers are speeding up the rollout of the scheme, previously announced by Sir Keir Starmer's government, by 18 months as part of efforts to tackle violence against women and girls (VAWG).

They are also offering more money for some forces to boost protection orders.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the previous plans were "too slow" and ministers should be "laser focused" on tackling such crimes.

One charity has welcomed the measures, but says they represent "only a small portion of what is needed" for victims.

The Home Office initially announced the plans last year and was due to have teams in place by summer 2029.

Burnham said: "The scale of violence and abuse suffered by women and girls in this country is unacceptable.

"We're taking action to accelerate the roll out of specialist rape and sexual offence teams, who will go after perpetrators, enforce strict new protection orders to protect survivors, and invest in programmes to intensively manage offenders to break the cycle of abuse."

Up to 10 police forces across England and Wales will also get a share of a £13.3m pot to boost the teams managing protection orders, where offenders are subject to electronic monitoring, exclusion zones and other measures, the Home Office has said.

Minister for Safeguarding Satvir Kaur said violence against women and girls was one of the "most critical challenges of our time" and the government was strengthening its response by "relentlessly pursuing perpetrators and helping victims live their life without fear".

The charity Refuge welcomed the changes, but suggested the government should go further.

Its head of policy and public affairs Ellie Butt said the measures "represent only a small portion of what is needed to ensure all survivors can access timely and effective support".

She said the charity hoped the announcement would be the "first step of many" in Burnham's plans to tackle VAWG, adding that protection orders were "highly underutilised" and "enforcement is often inadequate".

"Survivors often avoid reporting the abuse they've experienced to the police for fear of being disbelieved or undermined, so for protection order teams to increase uptake of these tools, genuine efforts are needed to build women's and girls' confidence in policing and ensure abuse does not go unreported," she added.

In December, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood described violence against women and girls as a "national emergency" as she announced plans for the specialist investigation teams.

She told the BBC at the time that the way police forces investigate cases was "too much of a postcode lottery".

The accelerated rollout comes as the prime minister has been facing pressure over the early release scheme, designed to avert overcrowding in the country's prisons.

Justice Secretary Alex Norris is expected to reveal the findings of a review of the scheme next week when MPs return to Parliament from their summer recess.

The plans were paused earlier in the summer, and the eligibility for the scheme was also changed, removing the right of those convicted of rape, serious child sex offences and grooming to have their sentences cut.

However, domestic abuse commissioner Nicole Jacobs said not excluding domestic abusers was "wrong and puts victims lives at risk".

She said earlier this month: "It is critical that no abuser is released in October unless I am confident that victims' safety is not being compromised."

articles.title: Anne Donaghy: Ex-council chief investigated in DUP mayor clothing probe
articles.summary: Anne Donaghy is one of three people referred to prosecutors for consideration over alleged misconduct in public office.
articles.body:
An ex-council chief executive is a subject in a police investigation into a former Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) mayor's clothing expenses.

Anne Donaghy is one of three people referred to prosecutors for consideration over alleged misconduct in public office at Mid and East Antrim Borough Council.

It is the latest case surrounding its handling of Freedom of Information (FoI) legislation after Donaghy was convicted on Wednesday of two charges over the deletion of an email to former DUP leader Arlene Foster.

Donaghy's solicitor told BBC News NI the allegations would be "met with the same robustness as this week's proceedings which are now under appeal".

The Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) confirmed a file has been submitted to the Public Prosecution Service (PPS) for consideration.

Police said the investigation was in respect of two women aged 56 and 42, and a 57-year-old man.

None of the three are the former DUP mayor whose expenses were examined.

The case centres on questions over clothing expenses claimed by Audrey Wales, 80, who was mayor between 2016 and 2017.

The Ballymena councillor spent more than £2,300, but the council did not disclose the full cost when asked for details in an FoI request.

Instead its response in 2019 said Wales had spent just £190.

The entire bill was only revealed in a second FoI in 2022.

In a statement in 2022, Wales said she had sent a cheque in 2019 reimbursing the council for most of the spending to stop "electorally motivated questions".

The cheque was received by Donaghy, but was never cashed.

Wales, who sent a second cheque in 2021 upon learning the first had not been processed, said that "at all times" she acted in line with "guidance from council officials".

The council in 2022 commissioned a Belfast-based firm to conduct an investigation.

It found the council's FoI response involved "a deliberate manipulation", according to a copy leaked to the Belfast Telegraph.

Donaghy has previously denied being involved in discussions about the FOI and said an email she sent referring to the cheque showed that she intended to cash it.

When asked at the time whether it was examining the case, the PSNI said detectives were continuing to "investigate suspected offences of misconduct in public office and under the Freedom of Information Act 2000".

In an update, a PSNI spokesperson told BBC News NI: "A file was submitted to the PPS in January 2025 concerning this investigation in respect of two females aged 56 and 42, and a 57-year-old man."

It is understood the investigation file relates to alleged offences including misconduct in a public office.

The PPS does not comment on any evidence in a file while it remains under consideration.

The case emerges after Donaghy was on Wednesday convicted of two charges connected to deleting or attempting to delete an email to prevent disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act.

The 56-year-old, of Clonmore Road, Dungannon, was fined £1,500. She was cleared of a third charge of trying to have an email deleted.

On Wednesday Donaghy's solicitor said she "maintains her innocence" and would "vehemently contest" the findings.

In a further statement on the clothing expenses case, her solicitor said: "These are allegations of some considerable vintage stretching back a number of years.

"If they ever materialise into anything then they will be met with the same robustness as this week's proceedings which are now under appeal."

Mid and East Antrim Borough Council has said it will "carefully consider the outcome and any implications arising" from this week's trial.

It added the council is "committed to the highest standards of governance, transparency and information management".

articles.title: How I beat my late-night shopping addiction
articles.summary: Younger generations are thought to be more susceptible to impulse spending. The BBC looks at ways to get it under control.
articles.body:
You may well have been there. It's late, you're scrolling on your phone and suddenly feel a strong urge to buy something - only to wake up the next day and regret it.

But what happens when those impulse buys become a habit rather than a one-off?

One global study suggests 7% of adults experience shopping addiction - an uncontrollable urge to spend despite the financial consequences - and younger women are more susceptible.

Ella Hewitt, from Liverpool, says her shopping addiction got so bad in 2021 that she was spending up to £700 a month on fast fashion she couldn't afford and sometimes never even wore.

"I didn't grow up with much money, so when I got a job I would spend my wages as soon as they hit my account," says the 24-year-old.

"That dopamine hit kept me shopping and in the world of social media there is just so much encouragement to do that."

She says she would often make purchases on TikTok or Instagram when she was "tired" or "bored", lured by the latest trends on her feeds.

She was working as an HR assistant in a school at the time and her spending meant she couldn't afford to move out of her family home.

"Horrified" by how much she was buying, she began using diversionary tactics to control her spending.

One was to put anything she felt like buying on a wish list and wait 30 days.

"If I still wanted it, I would buy it, but more often than not I'd find the urge had gone," she says.

Ella gave herself an imaginary budget of £1,000 each day to spend on imaginary purchases, which "scratched the itch" of shopping without the cost.

And she vowed only to buy something if she could afford to "buy it three times".

"Overall, I cut my spending by about 60%," says Ella, who now works as an ethical fashion influencer and plans to launch her own clothing brand.

"I'm not perfect. There are times when I will buy things because I want it. But I am way more in control."

The Ukat Group, which runs addiction treatment centres across the country, says it has seen more people with a shopping addiction and 90% are women.

It says there are various signs you may have a problem , such as your mood improving immediately after making a purchase, or feeling guilty or ashamed afterwards.

You may also lie to loved ones about your spending habit or have a home "full of items you don't need or use".

Wait 48 hours or longer before you purchase something. Often the urge will go

Delete saved credit card numbers and shopping apps

Write a shopping list before you enter a store or visit a site, and stick to it

Set a small budget for guilt-free treats, or create an imaginary one

Use up products before buying new ones; accessorise rather than buying brand new outfits.

Know your triggers: If you shop when you feel lonely, bored or stressed, try exercise or talking with a friend instead

Seek help: Citizens Advice, Stepchange, Christians Against Poverty and National Debtline can all offer advice on money problems.

Sources: The United Nations Federal Credit Union, Christians Against Poverty

'I would buy anything that was trending'

Dish Patel, 23, from London, says she was spending so much on clothes, food, make-up and skincare as a student that she "maxed out" her £2,500 overdraft and was "always broke".

Like Ella, she thinks she was making up for not having much money as a child, but the joy was always short-lived.

"The feeling you get when you open your new parcels is always amazing until the dopamine hit dies down and the cycle repeats."

Dish, who now works as a financial planner, says she would buy "pretty much anything that was trending" but her biggest vice was scrolling on shopping apps to pass the time.

'I didn't want to spend the money twice'

Then, she deleted shopping apps like Asos and Pretty Little Thing from her phone and removed ApplePay to make it harder to buy things in a single click.

She even started leaving her bank cards at home when she went to work.

"I would bring a packed lunch in and I would buy my train ticket on Trainline the night before... This basically put me in a habit of not spending a single thing and pre-planning my day to ensure I don't spend anything."

She also vowed that any time she wanted to buy something, she had to put the same amount of money into her savings or investments.

"It worked because I didn't want to spend the money twice."

Research last year from Vanquis, a challenger bank, found Gen Z shoppers make more impulse purchases than any other age group , closely followed by millennials.

And some experts say exposure to social media, with its targeted advertising, influencer culture and seamless one-click checkout, is fuelling the trend .

Money and Mental Health, a charity, also blames the design of online shopping sites for "minimising the friction around spending money".

It points to "pop-ups" that put customers under pressure to spend, and the inclusion of alternative payment methods like Buy Now Pay Later.

The BBC has contacted Meta, which owns Instagram, TikTok and Asos for comment.

articles.title: Pizza restaurants: Why pizza-making robots are not cutting it
articles.summary: A string of failures has sapped confidence that robots will take over production at pizza restaurants.
articles.body:
The "dough feeder". The sauce and cheese modules – even the pepperoni-sprinkler. All lay still.

A now defunct duo of robots were supposed to be churning out pizzas at a Moto Pizza restaurant in Seattle.

However, in May the pair were rendered "basically useless" when their supplier, Picnic, abruptly shut down. Technical support for the robots evaporated at that moment, says Lee Kindell, founder and chief executive of Moto Pizza.

He was left wondering what to do with the $160,000 (£118,000), cabinet-like machines and whether buying in pizza bots was really worth it.

"I don't know if I want to do a partnership again because of the failures," he says.

The robot pizza-making business has, it's true, been littered with sorry tales of overcooked promises and melting fortunes. Besides Picnic, other companies that have come and gone include Zume and Pazzi, which used robot arms to assemble pizzas, as well as Basil Street , a purveyor of pizza vending machines.

Although so-called fast food might seem an easy target for automation, it's proved harder than many expected. Plus, bringing robots into pizza restaurants could take away entry-level jobs in the hospitality sector. Is the future really filled with robotic pizza?

"We haven't yet seen any of the success stories materialise the way some people thought they would," admits Sara Senatore, senior restaurants analyst at Bank of America. Her employer has financial interests in multiple high street pizza chains including Papa Johns and Domino's.

Food preparation bots are sometimes clumsy – dropping ingredients in the wrong places at times, she explains. Conversely, "Humans are very efficient at making pizza."

But Kindell, despite his frustrations with Picnic, is surprisingly undeterred. He is a fan of full automation. "I want to be able to walk up to, let's say, a type of kiosk, put in your order, and it makes a fresh pizza," he tells the BBC.

Kindell, who once made all his dough by hand – until an elbow tendon injury forced him to investigate using machines instead, is now working on his own version of a pizza-making robot.

He declines to share details but the contraption will make square pan-style pies and that the machine is inspired by the way 3D printers work. If things go well, he says he could have a fully operational version of the device by the summer of 2027.

Given that he admits he has "no experience" in robotics, I question why he would want to invest in such a dicey business. Kindell says that failed pizza robot companies have nonetheless generated useful data and made strides in developing their technology. It's just a matter of time before someone gets these things to work, he insists.

On jobs, he claims that even "fully autonomous" pizza robots won't threaten workers. Kindell previously used Picnic's robots at T-Mobile Park, home of the Seattle Mariners, a baseball team.

Usually, he'd need about 10 people to make pizza in such a setup. With the robots that number fell to just two. But the other eight people were still employed, he says, in roles where they interacted with customers, and advertised the pizza around the stadium.

"We had so many more people able to hand out the pizza," says Kindell. "It was so much faster."

For some pizza robotics engineers, speed is certainly a motivator. Last year at the John Glenn Columbus International Airport in Ohio, Canadian firm Appetronix installed a 24/7 robotic pizza unit for the Donatos pizza chain.

Appetronix is working on newer versions of the technology that it claims will assemble pizzas at a furious pace. The goal is to eventually have a pizza sliding out of such machines "every minute", says co-founder and chief executive Nipun Sharma.

To that end, his team is investigating methods of depositing sauce onto a pizza base far faster than the 9.5 seconds currently required. "Think of it as a shower head that blasts the sauce in 1.5 seconds," says Sharma.

The company is even investigating lasers and ultrasound as potentially speedier methods of slicing pizzas than a traditional knife blade.

Many people enjoy hand-crafted pizza, though, I suggest. Doesn't a machine making your dinner take away the human connection we might otherwise feel with food? "What we're going after is a chain market," replies Sharma. "You want the pizza to taste the same every single time."

This divide, between businesses focused on repeatability, and those who promise a more artisanal, human-fronted experience, predates robotics. But it will likely shape how and where technology arrives in the world of pizza.

Five years ago, Paul Giannone – owner of Paulie Gee's pizza restaurants – vowed to Mashable that he would "never" use a robot. "That is still the case," he tells the BBC. "Our shops offer a dining experience with personal customer service a high priority."

Senatore says that human interaction is potentially an even more important factor today than in the past, including for restaurants that do decide to introduce pizza robots.

"It's a risky proposition to not have people," says Senatore. Pizza parlours could lose their "human touch", she adds, and potentially also frustrate customers should the machines go wrong while no-one is around to step in.

But expect new pizza tech to keep appearing. Not least because the meal-assembling robot companies that have seemingly disappeared are actually still influencing food start-ups. The intellectual property formerly owned by Zume – more than 300 patents – was bought up by Miso Robotics, of California.

"Their vision for robotic pizza making was really brilliant," says chief executive Rich Hull. "I just think they were a beat too early in the market." Customers weren't "ready" for robot-made pizza, he asserts.

Miso Robotics makes a French fry-cooking bot called Flippy, already in use in some US fast food restaurants. The Zume patents could help Miso Robotics expand Flippy's capabilities, suggests Hull, though he does not cite any specific example. "That's one of those things that we're going to be learning about," he says.

The natural cut-and-thrust of the fast food pizza business looks set to continue. Kindell remains set on automating pizza production.

"There is no doubt in my mind that there will be a fully autonomous pizza robot," he says. "It's just, who's going to do it first?"

articles.title: Russia threatens strikes on UK military targets, ‘catastrophic consequences’ over Ukraine
articles.summary: Russia threatened to strike British military targets inside and outside Ukraine after Moscow accused Kyiv of using Storm Shadow missiles against Donetsk.
articles.body: Russia warned Thursday that it could strike British military targets inside and outside Ukraine if Kyiv uses long-range British cruise missiles against targets deep inside Russian territory, according to reports. This came a day after Moscow accused Ukraine of striking a shopping center in Russian-controlled Donetsk with British Storm Shadow missiles, wounding civilians, including children. Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova said Thursday that Britain was "one step away" from becoming legally complicit in what she described as civilian-targeted "terrorism," warning that failure to change course would bring "catastrophic consequences," Reuters reported. US ALLY ON PUTIN’S DOORSTEP BRACES FOR WAR AS RUSSIA TENSIONS TAKE OMINOUS TURN "We have repeatedly warned that any British military installations and equipment in Ukraine and beyond its borders could be targeted in response to Ukrainian strikes on Russian territory carried out using British weapons," Zakharova said at a news briefing in Moscow. She urged British leaders to "immediately, in the most resolute and unequivocal manner, abandon the hostile, aggressive line" to prevent the conflict from escalating to an "entirely new level." British Prime Minister Andy Burnham visited Ukraine Aug. 24 for Independence Day, when he announced that a defense contractor could release classified information about British components used in the long-range SCALP cruise missile as Ukraine and France seek to establish assembly lines in Ukraine, according to the U.K. government. PUTIN 'PANICKED' AS DEFIANT UKRAINE MARKS INDEPENDENCE DAY UNDER RUSSIAN BOMBARDMENT The SCALP missile, the French version of Britain's Storm Shadow, can strike targets more than 155 miles away. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said the U.K. was "participating in the war" and "pouring fuel on the fire." A spokesperson for Britain's Ministry of Defense told Reuters London stood "shoulder to shoulder" with Ukraine and was committed to providing the equipment that Kyiv needed "to defend itself against (President Vladimir) Putin's illegal invasion." "Russia should be in no doubt about the resolve of this government to stand against Russian aggression in Ukraine and against the U.K. and our allies," the spokesperson said. UK'S BURNHAM NAMES TRUMP CRITIC ED MILIBAND FOREIGN SECRETARY; EX-THATCHER AIDE BRANDS PICK 'DISASTROUS' During his Kyiv visit, Burnham also hit back at Moscow, condemning Russia's "outrageous threats" and asserting that Britain's support for Ukraine would not waver. Russia also warned Britain Aug. 17 that it would pay a "price" after The Times reported Aug. 15 that British-made drones supplied to Ukraine were used to strike military and industrial targets inside Russia for the very first time. Britain's Ministry of Defense did not confirm whether British drones had been used in the strikes. Zakharova made the remarks as President Donald Trump downplayed concerns about a broader war, telling Axios in a phone interview Thursday he was not concerned Russia would attack a NATO member. US MILITARY PLANE LANDS IN MOSCOW, WITH KREMLIN CLAIMING IT HAS NO INFORMATION: REPORT Sergei Naryshkin, head of Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service, known as the SVR, confirmed Thursday that he met with CIA Director John Ratcliffe in Moscow earlier this week, Reuters reported. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Naryshkin characterized the meeting as routine, saying they discussed issues within the scope of their intelligence services, according to Reuters. Trump similarly described Ratcliffe's trip as "semi-routine," according to Axios. Fox News Digital has reached out to 10 Downing Street for comment.

articles.title: Camaru 2026 dá início a 10 dias de festa com mais de 15 shows, rodeio e exposições | G1
articles.standfirst: A 62ª Exposição Agropecuária de Uberlândia começa nesta sexta-feira (28) com shows de Gusttavo Lima e Diego & Victor Hugo. Organizadores ampliam o olhar para o público da nova geração.
articles.summary: A 62ª Exposição Agropecuária de Uberlândia começa nesta sexta-feira (28) com shows de Gusttavo Lima e Diego & Victor Hugo. Organizadores ampliam o olhar para o público da nova geração.
articles.body:
A espera acabou. O Camaru 2026 começa nesta sexta-feira (28) prometendo uma das maiores edições da história da exposição agropecuária de Uberlândia . Segundo o presidente do Sindicato Rural de Uberlândia, Thiago Fonseca, os números já apontam para o maior Camaru já realizado.

Até 6 de setembro, o Parque de Exposições receberá uma programação que reúne mais de 15 atrações musicais, rodeio profissional, torneios leiteiros, concurso de queijos, eventos gastronômicos, exposições de animais, provas equestres, debates voltados ao agronegócio e atividades para toda a família.

"Nós já tratamos esse como superior a 2025. Já é o maior Camaru de todos os tempos e não é só show, não é só rodeio. Nós vamos discutir temas importantes para o produtor rural, sustentabilidade, crédito rural, liderança feminina, cultura e várias outras atividades durante os dez dias", disse o presidente.

Arena de shows Camaru 2026 — Foto: Sindicato Rural de Uberlândia/Divulgação

A abertura da programação artística da 62ª Exposição Agropecuária de Uberlândia será com Gusttavo Lima e Diego e Victor Hugo. Ao longo da festa também passam pelo palco nomes como Zé Neto e Cristiano, Bruno e Marrone, Alexandre Pires, Ralf, Paraná, Pablo, Panda e Grupo Dos Rosa.

Responsável pela grade de shows, o produtor Marcelo Cunha destaca que a proposta foi montar uma programação diversificada para diferentes públicos.

"Neste ano conseguimos uma grade muito bem mesclada, reunindo artistas que dialogam com o público mais jovem, como esse Grupo Dos Rosa, que é um fenômeno e para o qual já temos mais de 10 mil ingressos vendidos", comentou.

Marcelo ressalta ainda atrações que marcam a edição, como o encontro de Bruno & Marrone e Alexandre Pires no dia 30 de agosto, o retorno da dupla Marco & Mário aos palcos após 12 anos e a aposta em outros artistas mais novos que são sucesso no Brasil todo, como os cantores Pablo e Panda.

Organização espera superar os números do Camaru de 2025 — Foto: Sindicato Rural de Uberlândia/Divulgação

Camaru - Torneio PBR — Foto: Sindicato Rural de Uberlândia/Divulgação

Além dos shows, o Camaru receberá pelo terceiro ano consecutivo uma etapa da Professional Bull Riders (PBR), principal liga de montaria em touros do país. As provas acontecem nos dias 1º, 2 e 3 de setembro, com portões abertos ao público.

Outras provas equestres que devem mexer com a emoção do público são a Prova dos Três Tambores e o Ranch Sorting.

Casa do Leite - Camaru 2025 — Foto: Nara Souza/Divulgação

A programação do Camaru também reforça o caráter agropecuário da feira. O Espaço do Produtor receberá julgamentos das raças Nelore e Girolando, palestras sobre reforma tributária, sustentabilidade, bioinsumos, crédito rural e liderança feminina, além do tradicional concurso de Queijo Minas Artesanal da região do Triângulo Mineiro.

Para as famílias, um dos destaques volta a ser a Fazendinha Camaru. Neste ano, o espaço terá acesso independente pelo bairro Santa Luzia e funcionamento diário, com expectativa de receber cerca de 15 mil estudantes em visitas guiadas, mais o público da exposição.

"A Fazendinha é um dos projetos mais tradicionais do evento. Ela permite que as crianças tenham contato com a realidade do campo e compreendam a importância do agronegócio para a cidade", destacou o secretário municipal de Agronegócio, William Alvorada.

Legião Rural levará country music ao 'Uai Sô' — Foto: Sindicato Rural de Uberlândia/Divulgação

O Camaru tem ações para o fortalecimento da programação cultural local. No dia 31 de agosto, quando os portões estarão abertos em comemoração aos 138 anos de Uberlândia, o público poderá participar do festival 'Uai Sô', que transformará o Espaço Estância 34 na 'Casa do Mineirinho'.

De acordo com a produtora cultural Antonia Nunnes, a partir das 12h, haverá feira de artesanato, produtos típicos mineiros e apresentações de catira do grupo Solas de Ouro. O espaço também apresentará contação de causos, shows regionais com Luiz Salgado e banda Legião Rural, e encerramento como convidado Renato Teixeira, que traz o show de sua turnê comemorativa de 80 anos.

"É um conteúdo que tem tudo a ver com a proposta do Camaru porque resgata a cultura mineira, as nossas raízes e a identidade do povo do interior em um lugar aconchegante, acolhedor, com um palco de 360º, explicou Antonia.

O festival dentro da exposição termina quando começa o show no palco principal. Os organizadores sugerem a doação voluntária de 1kg de alimento não perecível para quem for apreciar a programação. Os alimentos serão destinados a instituições que ajudam pessoas em vulnerabilidade.

A expectativa da organização é reunir milhares de visitantes em uma programação que une entretenimento, cultura, negócios e agronegócio em um dos eventos mais tradicionais de Minas Gerais.

Público Camaru 2025 — Foto: Sindicato Rural de Uberlândia/Divulgação

29 de agosto – Zé Neto e Cristiano + Hugo e Guilherme + DJ Netto

30 de agosto – Bruno e Marrone + Alexandre Pires com o projeto 'Pagonejo Bão'

31 de agosto – Marco e Mário no show de retorno – Entrada franca - Festival 'Uai Sô' das 12h às 22h com Legião Rural + Luiz Salgado + Renato Teixeira na Estância 34

1º de setembro - Rodeio PBR + Zé Mauro e Arthur - Entrada franca

articles.title: Quem era o turista mineiro encontrado morto em viagem de férias no CE | G1
articles.standfirst: João Luiz Pereira Ramos estava no Ceará pela primeira vez e já tinha passado por outras duas cidades cearenses antes de chegar em Paracuru. O corpo foi encontrado às margens do Rio Curu.
articles.summary: João Luiz Pereira Ramos estava no Ceará pela primeira vez e já tinha passado por outras duas cidades cearenses antes de chegar em Paracuru. O corpo foi encontrado no Rio Curu.
articles.body:
"Muito querido por onde passava" . É assim que vai lembrar Amanna Brito, cunhada de João Luiz Pereira Ramos, turista mineiro encontrado morto durante viagem de férias no Ceará. O corpo dele foi encontrado às margens do Rio Curu, em Paracuru , na região metropolitana de Fortaleza, nesta quinta-feira (27). João estava desaparecido desde última terça-feira (25) .

João tinha 32 anos e era natural de Mariana, em Minas Gerais. Ele estava sozinho em uma viagem de férias pelo litoral do Ceará e, antes de chegar em Paracuru, já tinha passado por Fortaleza e Aracati (na Praia de Canoa Quebrada). Essa era a primeira vez dele no Ceará.

João trabalhava como eletricista e era ex-aluno do curso de história na Universidade Federal de Ouro Preto (UFOP), em Minas Gerais — mas ele não concluiu a graduação.

"Ele era uma pessoa muito comunicativa, era muito carismático, atencioso, gentil. Fazia amizades muito fácil", lembra Amanna Brito, irmã de Luana Nunes, namorada de João Luiz.

A causa da morte do eletricista foi afogamento, segundo informações obtidas pela Prefeitura de Paracuru junto à Perícia Forense do Ceará (Pefoce).

Questionada, a Pefoce informou em nota que "foi acionada e os exames periciais necessários estão sendo realizados ".

Amanna disse que o cunhado tinha costume de ir para cachoeiras em Minas Gerais, mas acha que ele não sabia nadar muito bem.

João Luiz ficou hospedado no Hostel da Boneca, hospedagem na Praia de Canoa Quebrada, um dos principais pontos turísticos do Ceará. O estabelecimento lamentou a morte dele.

"Ele foi nosso hóspede neste fim de semana e foi embora na segunda, dizendo que seguiria viagem para Paracuru. Uma pessoa muito boa, educado, tratou todos com carinho e respeito . Durante a estadia, chegou a comentar que queria adotar outro cachorro. Estamos arrasados com essa notícia. Que Deus conforte o coração da família e dos amigos", disse o hostel, nas redes sociais.

A barraca de praia Freedom, em Canoa Quebrada, também lamentou a morte nas redes sociais: "Grande irmão. Passou pela Freedom Bar sábado [22]. Troquei altas ideias com ele , falamos da galera de [Belo Horizonte] BH. Parecia ser muito gente boa. Ele aproveitou a visita a seu amigo em Fortaleza para vir a conhecer a Freedom e Canoa Quebrada. Descanse em paz".

A Guarda Municipal de Paracuru informou que iniciou as buscas após ser acionada e recebeu apoio de populares , que indicaram a possível localização do corpo, nas proximidades do Rio Curu. Ao chegarem ao local, os guardas municipais encontraram o corpo de João Luiz.

A Prefeitura de Paracuru emitiu nota de pesar pela morte do turista, em que "se solidariza com familiares e amigos de João Luiz, expressando suas mais sinceras condolências e desejando força e conforto a todos".

Uma câmera de segurança registrou o momento em que João Luiz saiu do local onde estava hospedado para passear pela cidade de Paracuru ( veja acima ), na manhã da última terça-feira, dia em que foi visto pela última vez antes de desaparecer .

João havia chegado à cidade cearense na segunda-feira (24), quando se hospedou em uma acomodação pelo aplicativo Airbnb.

Conforme Luana Nunes, namorada de João Luiz, o mineiro estava viajando sozinho e saiu a pé para dar um passeio pela Praia da Pedra do Meio . Desde então, ele não teve mais contato com a família.

"Ele saiu para andar na orla da Praia da Pedra do Meio e avisou uns amigos que queria ver o encontro do rio com o mar. Uma moradora da cidade nos relatou que ele pediu informação para chegar ao local e seguiu andando sozinho, depois não foi mais visto", contou Luana Nunes, antes de receber a notícia sobre o corpo encontrado.

Turista mineiro João Luiz Pereira Ramos foi filmado saindo da hospedagem antes de desaparecer em Paracuru, no litoral do Ceará, na última terça-feira (25). — Foto: Reprodução

Ainda de acordo com a namorada do turista, João deixou todos os pertences na acomodação . Estava previsto que ele retornasse para Fortaleza na quarta (26) e, nesta quinta-feira (27), embarcasse para Belo Horizonte.

"Era uma viagem a passeio, ele era muito responsável e observador. Deve ter dado algum azar ou algo muito ruim aconteceu. Ele trabalhou o ano todo e juntou dinheiro para curtir essa viagem. Estamos despedaçados", disse a namorada do turista.

João Luiz chegou ao Ceará no dia 19 de agosto e essa era a primeira vez que ele visitava o Estado. — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

articles.title: Acordo com a Meta nos EUA abre frente em luta global contra danos gerados por redes sociais | G1
articles.standfirst: A Meta concordou em pagar até US$ 18 bilhões ao longo de uma década e limitar o uso do Facebook e do Instagram por adolescentes por meio de um acordo com quase todos os estados norte-americanos.
articles.summary: A Meta concordou em pagar até US$ 18 bilhões ao longo de uma década e limitar o uso do Facebook e do Instagram por adolescentes por meio de um acordo com quase todos os estados norte-americanos.
articles.body:
Facebook, Instagram e WhatsApp, plataformas da Meta — Foto: Richard Drew/AP

A decisão da Meta de restringir o uso das redes sociais por adolescentes nos EUA mostra que as empresas têm ferramentas para proteger melhor os jovens na internet, afirmaram autoridades australianas nesta quinta-feira (27).

A declaração ocorre enquanto o país enfrenta dificuldades para aplicar restrições semelhantes em seu próprio território.

O acordo de até US$18 bilhões da Meta com quase todos os estados dos EUA em relação aos danos causados pelas redes sociais aos adolescentes abriu uma nova frente na luta global dos governos para proteger as crianças e coibir o vício em plataformas como Facebook e Instagram .

Governos em todo o mundo estão tentando restringir o acesso de crianças a conteúdos online prejudiciais. A primeira proibição mundial do uso de redes sociais por menores de 16 anos aconteceu na Austrália, no final do ano passado .

A ministra australiana das Comunicações, Anika Wells, afirmou à Reuters que as empresas de redes sociais “têm à sua disposição as ferramentas para proteger os jovens contra seus recursos viciantes, mas optaram por não utilizá-las”.

Além da multa, a Meta concordou em limitar o uso do Facebook e do Instagram por adolescentes por meio de um acordo com quase todos os estados norte-americanos.

A empresa é acusada de ter desenvolvido as plataformas de forma a estimular o uso compulsivo por crianças. A Meta negou qualquer irregularidade ao concordar com o acordo.

O acordo traz mudanças radicais nas plataformas Facebook e Instagram nos EUA, incluindo a imposição de um limite padrão de duas horas dos aplicativos para usuários menores de 18 anos .

Na Coreia do Sul, o órgão regulador da mídia afirmou que algumas das medidas da Meta deveriam ser aplicadas a jovens usuários em todo o mundo, e não apenas em mercados específicos.

A Malásia, que proíbe menores de 16 anos de criarem contas em plataformas de mídia social, também acolheu a decisão como um sinal de que as plataformas devem ser responsabilizadas pelo que ocorre nelas.

A Comissão Europeia afirmou que aguarda que a Meta apresente mudanças para limitar os designs que geram dependência em suas redes sociais.

No início deste ano, o órgão já havia divulgado conclusões preliminares, indicando que a Meta violou a Lei dos Serviços Digitais (DSA, na sigla em inglês).

Em julho, a Comissão Europeia afirmou que o Facebook e o Instagram deveriam desativar a reprodução automática e a rolagem infinita por padrão, introduzir intervalos no tempo de uso e alterar os sistemas de recomendação para reduzir os incentivos que mantêm os usuários engajados — medidas que vão além do acordo nos EUA.

Em abril, a Comissão afirmou que a Meta não havia impedido que crianças menores de 13 anos abrissem ou mantivessem contas. O acordo nos EUA pode tornar mais difícil para a Meta argumentar que medidas mais rigorosas de verificação de idade são impraticáveis.

“Fomos muito claros. Esperamos uma gestão adequada do tempo de uso e um controle parental adequado nessas plataformas”, disse o porta-voz Thomas Regnier.

A aplicação das restrições na Austrália, no entanto, tem sido irregular até o momento.

As primeiras evidências sugerem que a lei tem sido prejudicada por sistemas fracos de verificação de idade.

Vários estudos, inclusive do órgão australiano regulador da internet, mostram que 80% dos menores ainda estavam nas redes sociais meses após a proibição entrar em vigor, em dezembro. Isso levou os parlamentares a dobrar a multa máxima e aumentar os poderes regulatórios.

Na Ásia, países como China, Coreia do Sul, Índia, Malásia, Indonésia e Filipinas também buscam uma supervisão mais rigorosa das redes sociais, bem como medidas restritivas, incluindo o bloqueio de supostos golpes e, em particular, a proteção das crianças.

O secretário do Departamento de Tecnologia da Informação e Comunicações das Filipinas, Henry Aguda, disse esperar que o acordo com a Meta ajude nas negociações com a empresa para discutir questões como abuso e exploração sexual de crianças online e golpes financeiros direcionados a filipinos.

O escritório de advocacia australiano especializado em ações coletivas Shine Lawyers informou que está em negociações com Mark Lanier, advogado que atuou na ação movida na Califórnia contra a Meta , sobre uma possível ação semelhante.

“Há anos, as famílias vêm perguntando se já foi feito o suficiente para proteger as crianças dos recursos das plataformas projetados para maximizar o engajamento”, disse Craig Allsopp, chefe de ações coletivas da Shine Lawyers.

“Estamos agora analisando se questões jurídicas semelhantes se apresentam na Austrália, inclusive se crianças e famílias australianas podem ter reivindicações relacionadas ao design, à operação e à promoção de plataformas de mídia social. Se famílias australianas foram afetadas, elas merecem respostas”, disse.

articles.title: Julian Newman abuse controversy explained as streamer responds after ex-girlfriend's viral videos
articles.summary: US Streamers News: Julian Newman is facing intense scrutiny after videos posted by his former girlfriend sparked allegations of abuse and quickly spread across social me.
articles.body: Julian Newman is facing intense scrutiny after videos posted by his former girlfriend sparked allegations of abuse and quickly spread across social media. The former basketball player and emerging streamer has denied presenting the complete picture, calling the posts “one-sided.” Newman says their relationship had become unhealthy before he ended it, while also claiming he has evidence that could offer a different account of what happened.Julian Newman abuse allegations surface after viral videosThe controversy began on August 25, when Newman’s former girlfriend, who uses the TikTok handle @janayaaberry, uploaded compilation videos titled “The real Julian Newman.” The clips appeared to show Newman arguing with her and seemingly slapping her wrist.One video included Newman saying:"You ugly ****! You want to disrespect me and not listen to me ever?!"The posts also contained images that appeared to show bruises or marks on her arms and legs. In another video, she accused Newman of punching her and confronted him about photographs allegedly found on his phone."I don't care, you punched me in my mouth, I'm a girl... You have photos... You have a *****'s *** in your phone."The allegations have not been independently established by the material provided. That distinction matters, especially in a fast-moving social media controversy where short clips can spread long before all the surrounding context is known.Newman responded by describing the relationship differently. He said he had supported his former partner for two years before deciding to walk away."My ex-girlfriend recently posted a video presenting a one-sided version of our relationship and events that have taken place. For the past two years, I supported her personally, professionally, and financially, and played a significant role in helping her build her own career. A few months ago, I ultimately made the decision to end what had become an unhealthy and toxic relationship."Julian Newman responds to abuse claims and says there are two sidesNewman also addressed events surrounding his August 22 fight against influencer Thiirty at Adin Ross’ Brand Risk 15 event. According to his statement, his former girlfriend allegedly appeared at several locations where he and his team were present, including a hotel where weigh-ins were taking place."This past week, she traveled across the country and appeared at locations where she knew I would be, including a hotel where my team and I were conducting weigh-ins. We made every effort to avoid confrontation and go our separate ways, but issues continued throughout the fight weekend."He then argued that the public had heard only one side of a complicated relationship."Since ending the relationship, I have chosen to move forward in my life, which includes dating other people. After seeing me on streams and dates, she chose to publicly share her version of events. However, there are always two sides to a story, especially when it comes to a complicated relationship."Newman claimed he possesses videos, recordings and messages that he believes could provide additional context. However, he said he does not intend to release private material simply as retaliation."I have videos, recordings, text messages, and other information that can provide additional context and tell a very different side of this story. I have no intention of publicly embarrassing her or releasing private material simply to retaliate. I genuinely wish her well, and hope we all can move forward separately. The timing of these accusations, particularly while I was on a date with Celina Powell, is difficult to ignore."For now, the dispute remains a clash between competing accounts. articles.title: New Israeli roadblocks entrench siege of homes in West Bank’s Qusra
articles.summary: After weeks of settler siege, three new Israeli gates around Palestinian homes in Qusra raise fears in West Bank.
articles.body:
Qusra, occupied West Bank – When Israeli authorities set up three new roadblocks at the Ras al-Ain hill in the northern occupied West Bank village of Qusra on Wednesday, Abdel Hakim Wadi knew he was about to lose access to his land below once and for all.

The roadblocks’ gates – large yellow and orange metal bars placed on two large concrete blocks – are infamous in the West Bank. They’re placed at the entrances of many, if not most villages, and have multiplied since Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza began in October 2023. The only ones holding the keys are the Israeli forces.

Israeli soldiers had already placed a gate at the main entrance of Qusra itself, forcing Palestinians traveling into the village to take alternative routes – but often find those closed as well.

Three homes in this area of Qusra have been besieged by Israeli settlers since August 9, attracting global attention and condemnation. Israeli forces have declared the area a closed military zone, but have effectively continued the siege, with locals trapped in their homes.

And now, instead of lifting the siege, the roadblocks erected by the Israelis have been placed in carefully-selected locations.

“They are pushing the Israeli settlers 100 to 150 metres away from [our] houses, but now they have established checkpoints,” Wadi told Al Jazeera. “[It is] a much more permanent siege.”

One of the gates was erected at the entrance of the house of Loui Ridi, a Palestinian-American who lives in Ohio, but who returned to Qusra to defend his property after the siege began. Israeli soldiers are stationed outside his home, which he has not been able to leave since his arrival on August 17.

Another roadblock is slightly further up the hill near a house under construction, and a third one is to the left side above a house that is being built.

All three barriers together encircle the top of the hill – and the homes on it – disconnecting it from the area below it.

Their presence also renders a road passing through the summit of the hill ineffective. The road not only connects the rest of Qusra with Ras al-Ain, but also links the village to the neighbouring villages of Talfit and Jalud.

Ridi said that Israeli settlers remain in the area surrounding his house, and the Israeli forces are still preventing him and his neighbours – a family including two little girls – from leaving and entering freely.

“We have been calling on the US embassy … or the international community to end the siege,” Ridi said.

Ridi has previously said that, despite the international condemnation of the actions of the Israeli settlers in Qusra – who cut off water and electricity from the besieged homes in their latest attack on a Palestinian community in the West Bank – little had been done.

“No one is doing enough on the ground,” he told Al Jazeera when he first arrived to Qusra from the US. “They’re talking, but there’s no action.”

Wadi’s land, which he has not had access to since the siege began, is located close to where one of the new Israeli gates was placed.

He told Al Jazeera that his land – nearly one hectare – is planted with more than 100 olive trees, in addition to other trees, including almonds and figs. There is also a water well that Israeli settlers have taken over.

“I see them bathing in the water that they’re taking out from the well,” Wadi said.

Wadi now fears that the gates will prevent him from ever setting foot to on the land, even if the Israeli authorities remove the military zone designation in the future.

He expects Israel to keep the siege in place, but in a different manner.

“They will put on a show that they have ended the siege but in fact all of what they’re doing is replacing the settlers with the army,” Wadi said.

Israel’s ultimate goal, Wadi said, is to grab more land in the West Bank, piece by piece.

articles.title: Malaysia to return 1,500 Rohingya refugees next month, despite safety fears
articles.summary: First phase of Malaysia’s repatriation plan will involve Myanmar nationals who are ‘willing to return voluntarily’.
articles.body:
Malaysia has finalised the first phase of a voluntary repatriation programme that will see at least 1,500 eligible Myanmar refugees return home on September 29, the government said.

Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced in July that Myanmar’s military-backed government had agreed to take back 5,000 members of the persecuted Rohingya minority amid rising tensions with local communities in Malaysia.

“The repatriation process will use two Myanmar naval warships and a hospital ship,” according to a Malaysia Home Ministry statement.

It said more than 4,000 individuals, primarily of ethnic Rohingya, will be channelled into the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) programme, while 5,000 others will undergo the voluntary repatriation process, as agreed with Myanmar.

There were 10,388 Myanmar nationals held at immigration detention depots by mid-August, the ministry said, with not all considered refugees.

Malaysia’s immigration department is working with the police to verify the identity, citizenship, immigration status, asylum claims and security background of those detainees by the end of the year.

Earlier this month, the government said it would not proceed with the repatriation if the refugees’ lives would be at risk upon return.

“Malaysia, as a responsible country, will not return the 5,000 Myanmar refugees if they would either be persecuted or their lives would be threatened,” Fahmi Fadzil, the Malaysian communications minister, said.

Human Rights Watch has said conditions for a safe, dignified and voluntary return to Myanmar do not currently exist, and warned that the Myanmar military continued to commit war crimes and crimes against humanity.

Malaysia has long been a safe haven for Rohingya fleeing persecution at home, even though it is not a signatory to the 1951 United Nations Refugee Convention and does not formally recognise refugee status.

Despite that, it hosts one of Southeast Asia’s biggest refugee populations and is home to more than 215,000 refugees and asylum seekers registered with the UN High Commissioner for Refugees, including more than 126,000 Rohingya from Myanmar, the country’s largest refugee community.

August 25 marked nine years since Rohingya were forced to flee Myanmar’s Rakhine state to neighbouring Bangladesh to escape a brutal military crackdown. Today, that number stands at more than one million.

The Rohingya are a mostly Muslim ethnic group who have lived in Buddhist-majority Myanmar for centuries. However, Myanmar does not recognise them as an official ethnic group, making them the largest identified stateless community in the world.

articles.title: Canadian council considers changing street named after Trump to Taco Avenue
articles.summary: A Canadian city council is considering renaming a street named after US President Donald Trump – and among the contenders for a replacement are “Obama Avenue” and “Taco Avenue.”
articles.body: A Canadian city council is considering renaming a street named after US President Donald Trump – and among the contenders for a replacement are “Obama Avenue” and “Taco Avenue.” In a unanimous vote on Wednesday, Ottawa City Council took a first step toward renaming Trump Avenue, a residential street in the Central Park neighborhood of Ottawa that has carried the president’s name for roughly 25 years. It is just one of the references to New York City in the neighborhood, which also has a Staten Way, Madison Park and even a Gotham Private. But amid the escalating trade fight between the two countries and Trump’s repeated jabs at Canada, some local councilors say they see the name as an embarrassment and do not want anything in Ottawa named after him. The council’s vote came just a day before Trump signed an executive order directing the US government to refer to Lake Ontario as “Lake America” – a move that echoes his renaming of the Gulf of Mexico as the “Gulf of America.” Ottawa City Councilor Tim Tierney told CNN that suggestions for the new name have included: Obama Avenue, Ontario Avenue, Canada Avenue, Beaver Avenue, Gulf of Mexico Avenue, Canada Goose Avenue, Pelosi Avenue and even Taco Avenue – a reference to the acronym Trump Always Chickens Out. Another suggestion: Rosie O’Donnell Avenue — a reference to the comedian and longtime Trump antagonist who moved to Ireland after his reelection. CNN has reached out to the White House for comment. Canada has plenty of other places bearing the Trump name, from lakes — including a Trump Lake in northern Ontario, which some online have already suggested renaming — to islands and a creek. But Trump Avenue is the only one actually named after Donald Trump, according to Tierney. Tierney said changing the street name wouldn’t happen overnight. More than half of the residents would need to support a name change, and a new name would then go through its own public engagement process. None of this is expected to happen until after municipal elections, scheduled for the end of October. And this is not the first time the Ottawa community has tried to change Trump Avenue’s name. In 2021, the 62 households on the street were asked whether they wanted to rename it: 21 voted yes, 21 voted no, and 20 didn’t vote at all. Those opposed weren’t necessarily Trump supporters, according to Tierney. Some simply didn’t want the hassle of changing their addresses, he said. While the issue had seemed closed following the 2021 vote, Tierney told CNN that the controversy over Trump renaming Lake Ontario as Lake America had put the issue back on the “front burner.” Still, he cautioned against letting the battle over names overshadow the much bigger tensions between the two countries. “The semantics of names, we can save that for another day in the future,” Tierney said. “Right now, I think our focus has to remain on trade and tariffs, something that this is just nothing more than a distraction from.” “We see the president doing something the same and it’s tired,” Tierney said. “Stop with the lame name game and let’s get back to the table.”

articles.title: Delhi model murder: Prime accused Imran arrested after encounter
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A day after a 21-year-old woman was found murdered in west Delhi’s Tilak Nagar, police apprehended the suspect Imran, alias Aqib, after a m.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A day after a 21-year-old woman was found murdered in west Delhi’s Tilak Nagar, police apprehended the suspect Imran, alias Aqib, after a manhunt across three states.Police said the victim, Muskan, was alone at home when she was attacked. Imran was previously involved in a 2021 case of assault and culpable homicide, cops said.An encounter broke out during the arrest operation, during which the accused sustained a gunshot injury before being successfully taken into custody. He has been shifted to a hospital and is now receiving treatment.Imran used to work as a trainer at the gym where Muskan also worked out. They had known each other for 1.5 years, a senior cop said.Police said her family had approached them in July against Imran for harassing and stalking her near her home. The family didn’t lodge a formal complaint.‘Planned murder’: Suspect came to house with knifeA senior police officer said the two had known each other for around one-and-a-half years. As per police sources, Imran had become suspicious that Muskan was speaking to someone else.The investigation has revealed that Wednesday, Muskan’s sisters had gone to Chandigarh, while her mother had stepped out to buy groceries when Imran arrived at the house. He entered around 5:40 pm, apparently in a friendly manner as he was known to Muskan. An argument subsequently broke out between the two, following which he allegedly attacked her with a knife. Muskan sustained three stab wounds to her abdomen. She was also strangled.Police said Imran remained inside the house for around 25 minutes after the attack and left around 6:05 pm. He allegedly took Muskan’s mobile phone with him while fleeing. The phone was later recovered by police from the roadside during the investigation.The family’s domestic help later entered the house and found Muskan lying in a pool of blood. She attempted to stop the bleeding by placing clothes over her wounds before rushing her to hospital. Muskan’s friend Aman said he received a call from her sister informing him that she had been stabbed. “I immediately reached her home, but she had already been taken to the hospital,” he said.Police sources said that the murder was pre-planned, as Imran had brought a knife with him to the house. Police have also obtained CCTV footage showing Imran moving hurriedly after the incident. Investigators are examining his movements before and after the murder to establish his whereabouts.During the investigation, police found Imran was heavily dependent on drugs. Following Muskan’s family’s complaint, he was sent to a drug de-addiction centre for some time in July. Her family alleged that the harassment continued for several months and Imran often followed her. While police claimed that the two had been in a relationship, Muskan’s family denied it.Investigators are also probing a meeting between Imran and Muskan at a hotel on Aug 20, days before the murder. Police are examining the circumstances of the meeting and other details that could shed light on what transpired between the two in the days leading up to the killing.According to an employee at the gym where Imran worked out, Muskan and Imran used to visit the same gym.The employee said Imran was removed around two months ago after he attempted suicide at his rented accommodation.The employee added that he had been working at the gym for the past four to five months, while Muskan had been coming there for around three to four months to work out.Here are more Raksha Bandhan wishes, Bhadra kaal and Shubh Muhurat from The Times of India.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news.
